proof_markdown:
## Theorem

Set `n=2^30`, `D=535,822,336`, and `T=n-2D=2^21`.

1. No positive-parameter complete schedule covered by Lemma 2.12 of [Hsieh–Mohanty–Zhang](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.12606v2) both has output length at most `n` and is certified by that lemma at bias `1/512`.
2. For an arbitrary mixed-length path lift of the accepted decomposition `C_*=B⊕<1>`, two explicit parity-class inequalities are equivalent to the lifted 1040-dimensional image being `T`-balanced. Thus they are exactly the missing certificate needed to append an all-one row and obtain dimension 1041.

### 1. Finite free-walk calculation

The complete schedule has `t=d²`,

`ell=κt^κr`, `M=n_0d^ell`,

and Lemma 2.12 supplies

`L=lambda^{ell(1-κ²/t^(1/4)-1/κ)}·2^{ell(κ+1)/κ}`,

where `lambda=max{2/sqrt(d),epsilon_0}` and `epsilon_0≤1/4`.

If `κ=1`, then

`L=(4 lambda^(-1/sqrt(d)))^ell`.

For `d≥4`, `lambda≤1`, so the parenthesized factor is at least 4. For `d=2`, it equals `4·2^(-1/(2sqrt(2)))>2`; for `d=3`, it is `4·(sqrt(3)/2)^(1/sqrt(3))>2sqrt(3)`. Hence `L>1` in every case and cannot certify bias at most `1/512`.

If `κ≥2`, then `d≥2`, `t=d²≥4`, and `r≥1` give

`ell=κt^κr≥2·4²=32`.

Thus `M=n_0d^ell≥2^32>2^30`. The complete-output construction therefore has the wrong exact length. Deleting most walks would change the distribution to which Lemma 2.12 applies and needs a new sparse-selector theorem.

### 2. Exact parity-split equivalence

Let the accepted message space be `U⊕<j>`, where `dim(U)=1039` encodes `B` and `<j,z_v>=1` for every base column `z_v`. For a path `q`, including repeated vertices with multiplicity, put

`g_q=⊕_{v in q}z_v`, `p_q=(number of visited vertices) mod 2`.

Then `<j,g_q>=p_q`. Partition the exactly `n` paths into `E={q:p_q=0}` and `O={q:p_q=1}`. For nonzero `u∈U`, define

`A_u=Σ_{q∈E}(-1)^{<u,g_q>}`, `B_u=Σ_{q∈O}(-1)^{<u,g_q>}`.

The signed sums of the lifted words indexed by `u` and `u+j` are respectively

`S_u=A_u+B_u`, `S_{u+j}=A_u-B_u`.

For real `A,B`,

`max{|A+B|,|A-B|}=|A|+|B|`.

The remaining nonzero message `j` has signed sum `S_j=|E|-|O|`. Consequently every nonzero lifted message has absolute signed sum at most `T` if and only if

`||E|-|O||≤T`,

`|A_u|+|B_u|≤T` for every `u∈U\{0}`.

The first inequality and `|E|+|O|=n` give

`D=(n-T)/2≤|E|,|O|≤(n+T)/2=n-D`.

This proves the claimed equivalence and shows why cancellation between even and odd paths is insufficient: both partial sums must already have total absolute discrepancy at most `T`.

### 3. Conditional augmentation

If a deterministic path family met these inequalities, no nonzero message could map to zero or `1^n`, since either word has absolute signed sum `n>T`. Hence the lifted matrix would have rank 1040 and would not contain `1^n`. Appending `1^n` would raise the rank to 1041. Every nonzero core word would have weight in `[D,n-D]`, and its complement would also have weight at least `D`; therefore the augmented code would meet the target distance.

Conversely, any dimension-1041 construction obtained by this path lift followed by all-one augmentation must make the core two-sided `T`-balanced, so it must satisfy the two parity-split inequalities.

### 4. Integrated architecture consequences

The strongest durable finite bounds now read:

| audited architecture | finite conclusion |
|---|---:|
| complete Ta-Shma cloud | augmented `k≤3` |
| complete one-edge scalar certificate | augmented `k≤838` |
| uniform Cartesian XOR clouds | augmented `k≤1025` |
| complete Gray register at rank 1040 | raw length `≥16,722,507,176,960` |
| HMZ complete free-walk schedule | `κ=1` certificate vacuous; `κ≥2` length `≥2^32` |

All are below, or fail to fit, the accepted dimension-1040 endpoint. The exact unresolved frontier is therefore a symbolically indexed sparse/non-Cartesian mixed-parity path family satisfying the parity-split system. This theorem is scoped and does not assert that such a family is impossible.

proof_steps.proof: For a binary word of weight `w`, its signed sum is `n-2w`. Thus weights in `[D,n-D]` are equivalent to absolute signed sum at most `n-2D=2^21`.
proof_steps.statement: The target two-sided allowance is exactly `T=2^21`, or normalized bias `1/512`.

proof_steps.proof: Substituting `κ=1` and `t=d²` gives `(4lambda^(-1/sqrt(d)))^ell`. The factor exceeds one for `d=2,3` by the displayed elementary estimates and is at least four for `d≥4`.
proof_steps.statement: The HMZ Lemma 2.12 certificate is greater than one when `κ=1`.

proof_steps.proof: Positive integers `κ≥2,r≥1` and `d≥2` give `ell=κ(d²)^κr≥32`; complete enumeration therefore has length `n_0d^ell≥2^32`.
proof_steps.statement: Every HMZ complete schedule with `κ≥2` exceeds the exact target length.

proof_steps.proof: The messages `u` and `u+j` have signed sums `A_u+B_u` and `A_u-B_u`, while `j` has sum `|E|-|O|`. Apply `max(|A+B|,|A-B|)=|A|+|B|`. These messages exhaust all nonzero elements of `U⊕<j>`.
proof_steps.statement: The parity-class inequalities are necessary and sufficient for a path lift of `C_*` to be a 1040-dimensional `T`-balanced core.

proof_steps.proof: If all paths have the same visit parity, one of `E,O` is empty, so `||E|-|O||=n>T`; equivalently, `j` maps to zero or all-one.
proof_steps.statement: No fixed-length path family can turn the full accepted code into an augmentable balanced core.

proof_steps.proof: The inequalities rule out a nonzero kernel and the all-one word. Appending all-one therefore raises dimension to 1041, and the two-sided weight interval ensures both each core word and its complement have weight at least `D`.
proof_steps.statement: Any explicit path family satisfying the parity-split system would yield a target-qualified dimension-1041 code.

theorem_statement: At `n=2^30` and `T=2^21`: (i) no positive-parameter complete schedule certified by Hsieh–Mohanty–Zhang Lemma 2.12 both fits length `n` and proves bias at most `1/512`; and (ii) for any mixed-length path lift of the accepted decomposition `C_*=B⊕<1>` with `dim B=1039`, the lifted image is a 1040-dimensional `T`-balanced core exactly when `||E|-|O||≤T` and `|A_u|+|B_u|≤T` for every nonzero `u∈B`. Thus fixed-parity lifts cannot improve `k=1040`, while a deterministic sparse mixed-parity family satisfying these inequalities would yield `k=1041` after all-one augmentation.
